To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rapidly increasing pervaseness of computers in human life requires the development of a new discipline that studies this phenomenon, which is called behavioural computer science, which is a unification of the behavioural sciences with computer science, which focuses on the modelling of human and artificial behaviour and their interaction, which is motivated by the future development of artificial intelligence, and which has the following agenda: (i) modelling human and artificial behaviour, and their interaction, (ii) modelling social influence and (iii) incorporating empirical

(1) BCS should be the discipline that studies the interaction of human and machine behaviours; (2) BCS is a new discipline and should be established as a new research community; (3) BCS should unify human and machine behavioural models, including social influence and (emotional) attitudes, to study human-machine interactions; and (4) BCS should use empirical evidence to update its behavioural models.

1) the development of information and communication technologies (ICTs) is increasingly dependent on a broad range of behavioural models; 2) these behavioural models should unify (model of) human and machine behaviour; 3) these models should be empirically based, rather than based on the rational actor model; 4) the development of such behavioural models can be facilitated by a broad range of research disciplines, including computer science, behavioural science, cognitive science, psychology, social science, and philosophy
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a broad discipline under the umbrella of Behavioural Computer Science, which aims to study human and machine behaviour as well as their interplay.
the study of how humans interact with computers and each other, and how this interaction is influenced by computer systems.

the study of human and machine behaviours, with an aim of developing a unified framework to model these behaviours and their interaction, and with a view to developing technology that is sensitive and responsive to human behaviour, and which can be trusted by humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BCS is the study of how to design, implement, and evaluate computer-based systems that interact with humans, and how to model human and machine behaviour to achieve this goal.
BCS should be a new discipline, with a focus on the interaction between humans and machines, where models are used for understanding and designing technology.

BCS is a new discipline that aims to study the interaction between humans and technology, with a focus on how to design technology that can adapt to the human behaviour, and how to influence this human behaviour.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the future of BCS will be a future in which humans and machines are indistinguishable, and thus the models used for studying their behaviour will also be indistinguishable, as we will be able to model human behaviour with artificial agents.

the future of BCS will be in the design and use of models of human and machine behaviours that are able to predict, explain and influence human and machine behaviours in an integrated way, in order to design and use information and communication technology in a way that will be beneficial to society.
the future of BCS is to be able to model and predict human behaviour in the same way that we model and predict machine behaviour.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the design of technology should be based on models that incorporate human behaviour, and that these models should be able to be used for both humans and machines, as well as to study their interaction.

BCS models should be able to model human and system behaviour, and their interaction, in a way that allows for a unification of the models, so that the behaviour of humans can be modelled in the same way as that of systems.
the design of information systems should be based on models of both human and machine behaviour.
